credits.creator: Sandy Kurt
credits.note: The ring of small circles touching the axes and diagonals, a lying and a standing square in each, and the choice of lines to ink follow this tutorial; our steps group the drawing differently and the text is our own.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Put the compass point on the centre and draw a circle.
Draw a horizontal line through the centre, then a vertical line at right angles to it. They cut the circle at four points.
Halve each right angle to get the two diagonals. The circle is now divided into eight equal parts.
Join the four points on the horizontal and vertical lines. This is the dynamic square, standing on its corner.
Join the four points on the diagonals. This is the static square, sitting flat. The two squares cross each other at eight points.

Draw the square that just touches the circle: a line at right angles to the horizontal at each side, and at right angles to the vertical at the top and bottom. This square is the tile that will repeat.

Put the compass on the crossing of the two squares just above the horizontal on the right, and open it until the circle just touches the horizontal and the diagonal. Keep that opening and draw the same small circle on the other seven crossings, on the centre, and on the four corners of the tile.
Through the middle of every small circle, rule lines parallel to the horizontal, the vertical and the two diagonals. Each small circle is now divided into eight.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Through the middle of every small circle, rule the lines parallel to the horizontal, the vertical and the two diagonals that the pattern runs along.

steps.text: Now the horizontal sides of the lying squares, one inside every small circle. Mark where each circle cuts the line through its middle that the side needs, and rule the side right across the tile; neighbouring circles often share the same long line.

Now the vertical sides of the lying squares, one inside every small circle. Mark where each circle cuts the line through its middle that the side needs, and rule the side right across the tile; neighbouring circles often share the same long line.

Now the slanting up to the left sides of the standing squares, one inside every small circle. Mark where each circle cuts the line through its middle that the side needs, and rule the side right across the tile; neighbouring circles often share the same long line.

Now the slanting up to the right sides of the standing squares, one inside every small circle. Mark where each circle cuts the line through its middle that the side needs, and rule the side right across the tile; neighbouring circles often share the same long line.

ink.text: Go over the lattice lines that form the pattern: around the centre an eight-pointed star, around it a ring of crossed bands, and in the corners the start of the next star.

pattern.text: Repeat the tile edge to edge. The corners of four tiles close into another eight-pointed star, and the bands cross between the stars as in a carved stone screen.

expect.note: Golden values computed by the engine; the pattern matches Sandy Kurt's drawing but no photo of a real example was found.
